title: The Passions and Self-Control
lead: How the Bible and the Jewish writings around it speak of desires, fears and anger, and of ruling them. The Greek philosophers called these the passions (pathē) and praised self-restraint; 4 Maccabees argues that reason trained by God's law masters them, while Paul speaks of crucifying the flesh "with its passions and its desires" and names self-control as fruit of the Spirit.

sections.b: Proverbs praises "ruling your own spirit" above capturing a town (Proverbs 16:32) and compares "a person who cannot rein in his own spirit" to "A breached city with no wall left" (Proverbs 25:28). The tenth commandment forbids craving itself (Exodus 20:17). In the New Testament, self-control is the last of the fruits of the Spirit (Galatians 5:23), Paul reasons with Felix about it (Acts 24:25), and 2 Peter 1:6 lists it in a ladder of virtues. Paul treats the passions as the flesh's: "Those who are Christ's have crucified the flesh, with its passions and its desires" (Galatians 5:24).
